findings:
CORRECTED 6-STEP ARCHITECTURE (what is true today, with the one caveat that steps 2-3 only apply to apps that already ship the hook):
1. The app author declares tools in the app repo: typed Python functions decorated with `@tool("Label")` in a module named exactly `<package>_lc_tools` (for example src/nucleisky_lc_tools/__init__.py), listed in construct.yaml extra_files. It imports only `labconstrictor_tools` and the standard library at the top; science imports go inside the function. Nothing is generated by the host from the notebook.
2. When the user runs the app's installer, the installer's post_install script (a hook each app repo carries; NOT in the template main today) checks that `<package>_lc_tools` exists, pip-installs `labconstrictor-tools` into the app's own environment from the GitHub main.zip archive (needs internet at that moment; not on PyPI), and runs `python -m labconstrictor_tools register --name <App> --prefix <prefix> --module <package>_lc_tools --version <v>`. If this fails the app still installs and only menuinst_debug.log warns.
3. 'Registration' is two JSON files in `~/.labconstrictor/apps` (override LC_HOME; also LC_APPS_PATH and a system folder): `<name>.schema.json` (generated by importing the app's module with the app's own Python, without running any tool) and `<name>.json` (name, display name, version, prefix, interpreter path, module). pre_uninstall unregisters. Hosts trust-check each entry and show skipped ones with a reason ('not available on this machine'). The website, napari and Fiji discover apps by reading these files, without starting Python.
4. A generic host plugin reads the cached schema and builds the form: napari builds a magicgui form inside one dock widget (groups, 'Show advanced settings', 'set' boxes for optional values, '  or file' rows, Run/Cancel); Fiji builds SciJava module items and lets Fiji's own input harvester draw the dialog (after one or two small chooser dialogs); QuPath builds a JavaFX form. Every image input accepts an open image/layer or a file. Hints such as groups, advanced and EnabledWhen are optional (Fiji ignores EnabledWhen).
5. On Run the host exports images as TIFF (or passes file paths) into a host-owned temp job folder and starts a separate worker process, `python -m labconstrictor_tools serve`, with the app's own interpreter (Appose-compatible JSON-lines protocol, progress, cooperative cancel, killed 3 s after Cancel if the tool ignores it). Host never imports app packages. napari keeps the worker alive 10 minutes (faster repeat runs; 'Restart worker'); Fiji starts a new one per run (about 12 s in the sandbox test).
6. Results return typed: images/labels as TIFF -> layer or window; tables as CSV; points and outlines (GeoJSON) -> points/shapes layers or ROIs/overlays; an affine -> a magenta additive placed layer (napari) or an overlay window (Fiji); numbers -> status line or Log; messages -> status/dialog. All front-ends write one log `~/.labconstrictor/logs/labconstrictor.log` and a run record `~/.labconstrictor/runs/<time>_<app>_<tool>/run.json` (napari 'Details…' shows it).

BIGGEST DISCREPANCY FOR THE PLAN: NucleiSky is not a bridge app today. Its tools exist only on the unmerged branch bridge-test, not in main, not in release 0.1.1, and its manifest says hosts: [notebook]. The same holds for CellTracksColab. The honest, shippable napari/Fiji example today is LabConstrictor Playground 0.0.1 (released 2026-10-08, installers for all three OS, hosts [notebook, napari, fiji, qupath], tool 'Feature tour' with five outputs, test expects 16 objects, registered as 'LabConstrictorPlayground'). risks: Spec step 2 ('installer registers the application') plus 'Experimental integration' framing would imply the downloadable NucleiSky installer works with napari/Fiji. It does not: NucleiSky 0.1.1 and template main have no registration hook; only a bridge-test build does.

Showing the NucleiSky 'Relocalize 2D' napari/Fiji views as a product feature contradicts NucleiSky's own labconstrictor-app.yaml (hosts: [notebook]) and the site's App Centre listing; the spec itself says not to change the manifest.

The word 'Experimental' understates the plugins' own warning ('untested and unlikely to be stable ... do not rely on it'); the site's Ecosystem copy already uses the stronger wording, so the demo would be inconsistent with the rest of the site.

The reference screenshots predate the current widget (no 'Copy as command', 'Details...' vs 'Details…', no points/outline layers, app/tool preselected), and the napari app/tool selectors have no visible labels; reproducing 'Application' and 'Tool' labels from the spec would be wrong. In current builds the tool dropdown order is by tool id.

Fiji is not one dialog: the demo must not combine App selector, Tool selector, Reference/Query and OK in a single window, and must not show Rescan apps, Restart worker or Details for Fiji. Menu text differs between the jar and script routes.

The result numbers (rotation 12.17, scale 1.0024, 429/9 nuclei, quad, 12.0 s) are from one AI sandbox run on a synthetic Gaussian-blob fixture; the fixture's true zoom is 2.0 but the tool reports calibrated scale about 1.0. Mixing the two would be an invented or confusing result.

The NucleiSky2DApp notebook is hand-written ipywidgets with Steps 0-3 and Options A/B; a 'Notebook view of the same tool as napari/Fiji' and the spec's 5-step notebook structure are not what the real notebook shows.

Docs disagree with each other: Fiji guide says both install routes give the same menu entry (false); HOST_FEATURES.md says Fiji macro recording works while the AI test failed it (D3) and the README says it is a prototype; docs say Windows .bat hooks never ran on real Windows while CI smoke-install on windows-latest passed on 2026-10-07.
